title.narrative: PFM Strategy, Action Plan adopted and implemented (Status)

description.narrative: PFM Strategy, Action Plan adopted and implemented (Status)

comment.narrative: Baseline not explicitly stated but inferred from the original formulation of the indicator.
logframe.

Following an initial scoping and diagnostic review of PFM in the province undertaken in consultation with Finance Department the Planning and Development Department and other interested stakeholders the PFMSPP team has prepared a complete draft PFM Financial Strategy and Action Plan. This plan has been reviewed at length with the stakeholders circulated to the donor community and is awaiting formal approval.

description.narrative: 2.1.2) Status of Balochistan Local Government Act (LGA) 2010 reforms regarding engagement of CIs, gender mainstreaming and district development forums;

comment.narrative: No amendments reforms in Balochistan LGA 2010 existed in 2017

The Balochistan Local Government Act section 87 amendment was passed by the provincial assembly of Balochistan on 15th August and assented to by the GovernorBalochistan on 22nd August 202On Page 1114 of the Bill a provision has been added into the Section 87 of the Act which reads as followingProvided that a Local Council subject to approval of the Local Government Board may engage Registered Community Based Organizations CBOs Community Institutions CIs in its local area development or execute such projects funded by the Donor Organizations Agencies

title.narrative: 2.1.3) Status of District PFM Assessments;

description.narrative: 2.1.3) Status of District PFM Assessments;

comment.narrative: Provincial Balochistan PEFA Assessment carried out but no district PEFA assessments in 2017
Target means that the District PFM assessments carried out in 2 selected BRACE districts

No District LG Sector PEFA assessments carried out TA prepared ToR District LG Sector PEFA District PEFA can be conducted after COVID19 lock down fully lifted in 2021 TA and OPMPFMII teams continued deliberation on PFEA and in a meeting on 10092021 concluded that there was no need to conduct selected District PEFA assessments as the District FRs are not in place yet and therefore no baselinereference is available. In follow up meetings with OPM it was agreed that TA with OPM will conduct capacity assessments of District Public Expenditure Financial Accountability in the LG Sector and of Expected Strengths Weaknesses of the District Financial Regulations FRs under the proposed GoB CLLG Policy this assessment will support the adoption of the proposed GoB CLLG Policy and regulate its implementation at District level through the JDDC by June2022

comment.narrative: Provincial PEFA findings showed low scores of all PFM Indicators and PFM Assessment Reports show weak district PFM capacity in July2017 Baseline
District PFM SWOT assessments completed in 2 BRACE Districts in Dec2022

OPMPFM project conducted 201819 capacity assessments followed by specific PFMFR trainings TA has not conducted provincial l or district capacity assessment exercises except capacityassessment BRDA TA consults BRACE MTREMM on their findings of capacity of BRACE stakeholders mainly RSPs and CIs TADCADC deployed in Dep Comm Offices provide adhoc capacity support to DC in selected operational tasks and facilitates JDDC meetings BRDA Capacitybuilding Workplan has been worked out by LGRDDBRDATA and its implementation will start from Q12022.

OPMPFM project conducted 201819 capacity assessments followed by specific PFMFR trainings TA has not conducted provincial l or district capacity assessment exercises except capacityassessment BRDA TA consults BRACE MTREMM on their findings of capacity of BRACE stakeholders mainly RSPs and CIs TADCADC deployed in Dep Comm Offices provide adhoc capacity support to DC in selected operational tasks and facilitates JDDC meetings BRDA Capacitybuilding Workplan has been worked out by LGRDDBRDATA and its implementation will start from Q12022.

description.narrative: 2.2.3) Status of capacity building with BRDA for GoB provincial/local authorities in support of CLLG policy;

comment.narrative: TA with BRDA designs and implements part of BRDA CB Plan that enhances capacity provincial local government authorities to implement the GoB CLLG policy

No progress due to COVID lock down Q3Q4 2020 only a limited number of virtual Assessments were held initial discussion on BRDA Curriculum being triggered through the DC Course which is organised by TA through BRDA TA continue to make efforts towards the BRDA training curriculum for CD LGRD and CMCE approaches. In this regard the capacity building plan provides detailed actions to be implemented provided on feedbacksigning of MoU with BRDA from LGRDD. TA has fully engaged BRDA Faculty in DC Training Course total 04 training courses were conducted at BRDA with participation of lecturers from BRDA. The engagement of BRDA Faculty includes facetoface discussion on different topics covered 04 trainings development of training modules presentation handouts and practical delivery of session during the trainings

comment.narrative: The TA District Coordination DC Courses engage 7 stakeholders from each district to become change agents in their district which is 10 of a critical mass of 50 stakeholders per district that need to be reached and mobilised

No progress due to COVID19 lockdown Q3Q4 2020 only a limited number of virtual initial discussion on BRDA Training Curriculum and Training Calendar The DC Course for 57 District staff held at the BRDA is to restart in Q22021. NOTE these district staff are to function in a limited way as ToTChange Agents after they return to the districts TA formulated the Capacity Building Plan with BRDALGRDD and it covers the BRDA Training for provincial LG Councils LG Staff representatives CIs aspects which are subject to implementation during Q12022 given the feedbacksigning of draft MoU with BRDA submitted to LGRDD.

comment.narrative: BRDA activates sustainable training technical exchanges twinning linkages with local institutes rural development academies other provinces and international organisations Hague Academy for Local Governance

No progress and due to COVID19 global lockdown in 2019 contact established with Hague Academy for Local Governance HAfLG No Exposure Visits could be arranged due to COVID lock down with other Provinces Pakistan Academy for Rural Development TA is making efforts to develop Twinning linkages between the BRDA and European local government associationsnetworks and training institutions for tapping technical resources and capacitybuilding providing technical inputs for designing course modules introduction of new approaches to transfer of knowledge providing support for production of manuals as part of the BRACE TA BRDA Capacity building programmeAs a followup to the ongoing contacts and exchanges reactivated in Q32021 with the Hague Academy of Local Governance HafLG in the Netherlands the TA prepared an Action Memo outlined the main issues to the pursued. The Academy is a globally reputed institute that provides capacitydevelopment training Open Courses that are directly related to the CLLG Policy Reforms that the TA and GoB are pursuing under the BRACE Programme.

LGRDD has been approached for revised SNE positions and in Q12021 number increased from 7 to 14 proposals for adjustment to RoB BRDA allowing more autonomous role as CBtraining provider COVID lockdown in Q3Q4 2020 caused only a limited number of virtual meetings with BRDA DG and staff to discuss BRDA RoBCapacity TA formulated the Capacity Building Plan with BRDALGRDD and it covers the BRDA financial management and budget sustainabilityautonomy aspects which are subject to implementation given the feedbacksigning of draft MoU submitted to LGRDD

description.narrative: 2.3.3) Status of capacity of the BRDA faculty and pool of trainers and researchers with regard to community led development approaches;

comment.narrative: BRDA staff capacity building plan formulated and implementation initiated

No progress made due to COVID Lockdown Q3Q4 2020 only limited virtual meetings held with BRDA DG to discuss BRDA staff strength positions and specializations in Q12021 number SNE increased from 7 to 14 TA has finalized the Capacity building plan with BRDALGRDD which provides detailed plan of action on BRDA faculty and pool of trainers and research which is subject to the signingfeedback of draft MoU TA continued engagement of BRDA faculty in district coordination training course s far 04 trainings to build the capacity and to create a pool of trainers and researchers among the BRDA existing team. This includes face to face discussion with the BRDA Faculty on different topics covered during the DC Training course development of training modules presentation handouts and practical delivery of session during the trainings.

title.narrative: 2.5.2) Status of Joint BRACE Communication & Visibility (C&V) Strategy and Action Plan;

description.narrative: 2.5.2) Status of Joint BRACE Communication & Visibility (C&V) Strategy and Action Plan;

comment.narrative: Common BRACE CV Strategy developed and implemented

TA took lead to formulate BRACE CV Strategy Dec 2019 TA took lead in updating BRACE CV Strategy Dec 2020 finalised with RSPs TA took lead in CV Action Plans of RSPs TA GoB Stakeholders Dec 2020 TA assisted BRACE programme to develop the CV Strategy and action plans during 2020 and the same has been updated during Q12021. TA has been able to activate the CV Working Group and by Jan2022 02 meetings are held. TA has coordinated with LGRDD to seek the CV Committees nomination from GoB. The Nomination from LGRDD has been received on 11012022.

title.narrative: 2.5.3) Status of BRACE Gender Mainstreaming Strategy (GMS) Strategy and Action Plans;

description.narrative: 2.5.3) Status of BRACE Gender Mainstreaming Strategy (GMS) Strategy and Action Plans;

comment.narrative: BRACE Gender Mainstreaming Strategy Action Plans finalised with RSPs and GoB and prioritised 10 GMS actions implemented for the latter

TA took lead to formulate the BRACE Gender Situation Analysis 2019 TA took lead to formulate Joint BRACE IPs GMS Strategy delays in 2020 due to COVID lock down finalisation GMS Strategy reset for 2021 BRACE TA to lead GMS Action Planning with selected GoB BRACE Stakeholders LGRDD PDD FD WDD SWD The GMS strategy was updated In June 2021 GMS Action Planning Workshop which accumulated specific GMS actions for 5 GoB departments with the LGRDD WDD SWD FD and PDD The EUD recommended and communicated to GoB for specific GMS short term assignment to be implemented by BRACE TA TA has activated GMS assignment to implement the 10 GMS actions 2 with each GoB Department while WDD to technically lead the assignment and through Interviewtest for GMS consultant the process at its conclusion to initiate the assignment and complete in first half of 2022

comment.narrative: TA Action Research on Theory of Change and District Development Strategy Plan conducted and Action Memos on training on District Development Strategy Plan and local government sector plan assignment drafted

No specific BRACE LG sector governance studies available except analyses in BRACE DoA ToR The ToC Exit Strategy and PEA assignments are to provide analysis on Balochistan LG Sector Governance ToC Assignment Report completed Dec 2020 except closure dissemination workshop TA has been making efforts to conduct Governance policy and legal research studies. Action researches conducted to formulate the CLLG Policy and implementprogress the 5 result areas BRDA Capacity building assessment conducted District Development Strategy and Plan assignment Situational analysis of district development forums Policy reforms etc.

title.narrative: Percentage of population, segregated by gender, in the targeted areas brought into organised fold through formation of COsVOsLSOs (threetiered) echelons.

description.narrative: Percentage of population, segregated by gender, in the targeted areas brought into organised fold through formation of COsVOsLSOs (threetiered) echelons.

comment.narrative: Baseline not explicitly stated. Value is set at zero at the start of the project as the indicator measures results outputs arising from the provision of services by the project.
At least 70 population in the targeted areas is brought into organised fold

A total of 14110 HHs were organizedadopted into 926 Community Organizations COs 677 men and 249 women COs 18 against the year one target of 5150 COs and 5.6 against the overall target of 16531 COs. Furthermore the COs were federated in 121 VOs 99 men 22 women against the year one target of 875 which is 14 achievement against the firstyear target and 5 against the overall target of 2685. Value for reporting related to COs 5.6 against the overall target. Result on VO is very close to the result on COs.

title.narrative: Number of village and UC development plans developed in partnership with local authorities

description.narrative: Number of village and UC development plans developed in partnership with local authorities

comment.narrative: Baseline not explicitly stated conventionally set at zero at the start of the project as the indicator measures results outputs arising solely from the provision of services by the project.

Target is not stated in the logframe which is simply stating 100 community organisations have developed Village Development Plans VDPs and Union Council Development Plans UCDPs in partnership with local authorities. However Target is mentioned on p. 29 of the first Interim report of BRSP Component Output 2685 VDPs and 211 UCDPs developed in partnership with elected representatives and local authorities. Total 2896 development plans.Target for BCDP component is not found. These plans are to be prepared for implementation in the frame of the BRACE program.

BRSP Component Micro Investment Plans MIPs were prepared for 12902 HHs which is 33 of the annual target of 38625 and 5 against the overall target of 247956. Due to delay in PSC and Social Mobilisation process no Village Development Plans VDPs and Union Council Development Plans UCDPs were prepared.BCDP already developed 300 VDPs and 39 UCDPs prepared under BCDP has been reviewed in light BRACE Programme inputs and are in the process of updating. Total 339 development plans.These plans are to be prepared for implementation in the frame of the BRACE program.

title.narrative: IPs develop and follow a common Communication & Visibility Strategy (Status)

description.narrative: IPs develop and follow a common Communication & Visibility Strategy (Status)

comment.narrative: Baseline not explicitly stated but inferred from the original formulation of the indicator.
Target is expressed in the definition of the indicator.

To ensure a wellcoordinated and uniform communication and visibility CV of the Programme RSPN in consultation with BRSP and NRSP and inputs from the TA and EU developed a draft Communication and Visibility CV strategy for the grant component of BRACE Programme. The strategy will be submitted to EU for approval in second quarter of year two. On the basis of draft CV strategies and with guidance from Communication and Visibility in EUfinanced external actions Manual implementing partners ensured standardised communication and visibility of the Programme.

title.narrative: IPs follow a uniform monitoring system (Status)

description.narrative: IPs follow a uniform monitoring system (Status)

comment.narrative: Baseline not explicitly stated but inferred from the original formulation of the indicator.
Target is expressed in the definition of the indicator.

the ME framework developed by RSPN provides a uniform monitoring system to Programme implementing partners with the following processes. In order to report on Programme performance a set of common Key Performance Indicators KPIs have been developed. BRSP and NRSP collect data on the KPIs on standardised formats and feed into a webbased MIS developed by RSPs with assistance from RSPN. The central dashboard develop by RSPN consolidates data from both the implementing partners and produce KPIs reports. Overall Programme wise districtwise tehsil and UC wise progress can be tracked in real time through this system. Programme monitoring plan detailed result matrix project monitoring matrix support and guide the overall monitoring system of the Programme.

title.narrative: IPs follow uniform, but contextualised, implementation strategies for the various components of the programme

description.narrative: IPs follow uniform, but contextualised, implementation strategies for the various components of the programme

comment.narrative: Baseline not explicitly stated but inferred from the original formulation of the indicator.
Target is expressed in the definition of the indicator.

RSPN has developed uniform but contextualised implementation strategies and related guidelines including Programme Implementation Manual PIM common gender sensitive ME framework and reporting mechanism on Key Performance Indicators KPIs Poverty Scorecard PSC survey Manual socioeconomic baseline and end line survey approach and methodology Community Awareness Toolkit CAT Communication and Visibility Strategy for the BRACE Programme during year one. Staff from BRSP NRSP and relevant departments of the GoB including from Local Government Rural Development Department Planning and Development Department Social Welfare Department and Women Development Department were trained to effectively implement these strategies.

title.narrative: Implementing Partners (IPs) develop a common results framework agreed with GoB (Status).

description.narrative: Implementing Partners (IPs) develop a common results framework agreed with GoB (Status).

comment.narrative: Logframe states none.
Target is expressed in the definition of the indicator.Logframe states Preparation phase harmonised systems developed and adopted and staff trained.

RSPN in consultation with implementing RSPs BRSP and NRSP ME and Programme staff developed a common and a uniform ME framework and quality assurance and control mechanism on common Key Performance Indicators KPIs for the BRACE Programme in the inception phase to ensure that the Programme results are monitored measured reported according to the guidelines and processes given in the PIM. The ME framework spells out the key functions of monitoring and evaluation and determines roles and responsibilities for the RSPN and RSPs ME teams in implementing programme functions. The framework provides detailed matrices including the Detailed Results Matrix DRM and Project Monitoring Matrix PMM that build on the overall BRACE Programme logframe and being used for elaborating what to monitor and how to track programme implementation progress. The ME framework was reviewed with RSPs and Government representative from Planning and Development Department in fiveday ME training workshop held in November 2017 and their feedback has been incorporated. The GOB accepted the ME framework in the training workshop in which GoB officials.
